 More ships attacked in Persian Gulf, oil prices rebound slightly after post-midterm plunge

 Tucker Reals ,

 Add CBS News on Google 
 Follow updates on the war in the Middle East for Friday, Nov. 6, here . See ea rlier developments below. 
 What to know about the Iran war:
 Oil prices fell sharply after the midterm elections, as markets appeared to hope the results might push President Trump toward a deal to end the Iran war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Commercial ships in the region continue coming under attack, however, and hitting sea mines , according to Iranian authorities. 
 As a senior Iranian security official met Thursday with Russian President Vladimir Putin at the Kremlin amid uncertainty over Mr. Trump's next move, Moscow warned Russian citizens not to visit Iran, citing the "risk of a new escalation." 
 Oman said Thursday it was still in talks with Iran aimed at creating a system for the nations to jointly control traffic through the vital shipping lanes of the strait, which the Omani foreign ministry said could "end the state of war and prevent renewed confrontations in the region." 
 New Updates
 3:55 AM
 Saudis say coalition intercepted 2 missiles launched by Houthis
 The Saudi-led coalition said on social media Fri day that its air defense systems intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by Houthi rebels toward Najran, a major city in southwestern Saudi Arabia.
 "Debris fell as a result of the interception, and damage assessment is underway," the statement said.
 By
 Brian Dakss 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-midterms-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-26cae232 
 link copied 
 3:43 AM
 Iran says 2 tankers hit mines, caught fire in and near Strait of Hormuz
 Iran's Revolutionary Guards said in a statement carried by state media Friday that two oil tankers hit mines and caught fire in and near the Strait of Hormuz, a day after Tehran claimed five other tankers had met similar fates. 
 "Two violating oil tankers — one east of the Strait of Hormuz and the other within the Strait itself — that attempted to transit via an unauthorized route struck mines," Iran's powerful Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said in a statement carried by state TV and the semi-official Tasnim news agency.
 "These two tankers had deactivated all their navigation and identification systems. Supported by the aggressive and terrorist U.S. military, they attempted to exit the Strait of Hormuz via an unauthorized path; however, upon striking mines, they caught fire and were immobilized," the statement added. 
 On Thursday, Iranian media reported that five oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz in similar incidents. 
 There has, however, been no confirmation of any of these incidents from maritime officials.
 Since the outbreak of the Middle East war on Feb. 28, Tehran has sought to limit traffic through the strategic waterway, which normally carries oil that amounts to one-fifth of global consumption. In response, the U.S. imposed a blockade on Iranian ports and has escorted tankers through the strait. Ships turn off their identification and navigation systems to try to avoid being detected.
 The U.S. Central Command said last month that it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via Hormuz since summer and recently said all mines had been cleared from the vital waterway.
 CBS/AFP 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-midterms-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-bee28815 
 link copied 
 3:04 PM / November 5, 2026
 Putin, Iran's security chief discuss building oil pipeline from Russia to Iran
 Russian President Vladimir Putin received Iran's security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, in Moscow Thursday to discuss strengthening ties between their two countries, including a pipeline to import Russian gas.
 Speaking to journalists after their meeting, Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, called it "an extremely important exchange," according to remarks reported by the Iranian embassy.
 "During the meeting with Mr. Vladimir Putin, discussions were held regarding the construction of gas pipelines from Russia to Iran," said Rezaei, Iranian state TV reported.
 He noted the aim was to enable Iran "to address its own gas shortages while also facilitating the sale of Russian gas to neighbouring countries."
 While a major producer, Iran has long suffered shortages of natural gas, essential for powering heating systems, which have been exacerbated by the war with the United States and Israel.
 During the most intense phase of the fighting, which lasted nearly 40 days, the U.S. and Israel struck key Iranian infrastructure including natural gas refineries, according to Tehran.
 By
 AFP 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-midterms-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-6361c8dc 
 link copied 
 2:43 PM / November 5, 2026
 Iranian foreign minister talks to counterparts from several Middle East countries
 Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi spent much of the day on calls with his counterparts from several Middle Eastern countries, including Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Turkey.
 In total, Araghchi held calls with nine different countries in the Middle East. Few details were shared about what was discussed on the calls, simply nodding to "diplomatic efforts to maintain stability in the region."
 Notably, Pakistan was one of those countries involved as they have been very closely involved as mediators in U.S.-Iran peace talks. Araghchi spoke to their foreign minister, Ishaq Dar, on Thursday evening.
 Araghchi also spoke to Saudi foreign ministers Faisal bin Farhan and Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman, despite accusations of Iranian involvement in attacks on that country by the Houthi militia in Yemen. 
 By
 Mark Osborne 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-midterms-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-8d875778 
 link copied 
 1:30 PM / November 5, 2026
 Trump administration held talks with Iran on deporting Iranians during the war, AP reports
 President Trump's administration held secret talks with Iran on deporting Iranians even as the war there dragged on, court documents obtained by The Associated Press show.
 The court documents unsealed Thursday show the Republican administration as recently as mid-October said it had plans to deport the Iranians through an unnamed third country, although it was unclear when it intended to do so. The judge in the case ordered the government to give the court 24-hour notice of any finalized plans to deport Iranians to Iran or to any other country and five days' written notice before any such deportation is carried out.
 The documents show the administration maintained contacts with Iranian officials during the war over the removals, specifically for submitting travel documents and figuring out "possible avenues for removal."
 "We are at war with a country where the President of the United States has said, as recently as two or three days ago, if not yesterday, that it is essentially lawless ... A country that is an enemy of the United States, according to the current president. A country that, according to our president, murdered tens of thousands of protestors," Judge Ana Reyes said according to the Oct. 15 transcript.
 "And what you're telling me is that the United States of America is going to send individuals back to that region, facing what you and I and everyone who would ever look at this would know would be, at a minimum, a serious threat of certain death."
 "Yes, your honor," Justice Department attorney Dimitar Georgiev-Remmel said. "The government is executing lawful orders of removal."
 The Department of Homeland Security did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
 By
 The Associated Press 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-midterms-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-91e53f69 
 link copied 
 12:52 PM / November 5, 2026
 Houthi drone disrupts traffic at Saudi airport, group says
 The Houthis took credit for disrupting travel using a drone at King Fahd International Airport on Thursday.
 "We targeted King Fahd International Airport in Dammam using a drone and our operation caused a disruption of air navigation at the airport," Houthi spokesperson Yahya Saree said on X.
 The city of Dammam, which is located in the oil-rich eastern part of Saudi Arabia, and King Fahd airport have been regular targets for Houthi attacks. Multiple drones have disrupted traffic at the airport this week, according to past announcements.  
 Two people were killed in a Houthi strike on King Fahd airport on Oct. 22.
 By
 Mark Osborne 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-midterms-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-1249a333 
 link copied 
 12:01 PM / November 5, 2026
 3rd U.S. aircraft carrier strike group heading for Mideast to make stop in Singapore, delaying arrival
 The USS Theodore Roosevelt aircraft carrier and its associated strike group will make a port call in Singapore Friday and will not reach the Middle East for at least another two weeks, a U.S. official told CBS News on Thursday. 
 There are already two carrier strike groups in the region and, which officials say is sufficient firepower to execute any commands issued by President Trump.
 Mr. Trump has not signaled yet, in the wake of the U.S. midterm elections, whether he intends to order major new strikes on Iran — an option he kept on the table with repeated statements ahead of Tuesday's voting.
 By
 Charlie D'Agata 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-midterms-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-caa16ee0 
 link copied 
 11:20 AM / November 5, 2026
 Oil prices rebound slightly after huge drop in wake of U.S. midterm elections
 The initial knee-jerk reaction to the U.S. midterm election results faded a bit Thursday.
 The price of a barrel of Brent crude oil, considered the international standard, rose 2.2% to $96.70, recovering a chunk of its nearly 9% drop from the day before. 
 Uncertainty still reigns about what will happen in the war with Iran and when the global energy industry can return to normal.
 CBS/AP 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-midterms-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-43a73238 
 link copied 
 11:10 AM / November 5, 2026
 As top Iranian official meets Putin, Russia warns citizens not to visit Iran, citing "risk of a new escalation"
 Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, met Thursday in Moscow with Russian President Vladimir Putin to deliver a message from Iran's supreme leader, according to the Iranian government. 
 They met amid uncertainty over President Trump's next move on Iran in the wake of U.S. midterm election results that represented a major rebuke of his policies, including, he has admitted, the decision to launch the war with Iran alongside Israel more than eight months ago.
 Mr. Trump said repeatedly ahead of the Tuesday vote that he had yet to make a decision on whether to order major new attacks on Iran or to agree a deal to end the war, which Tehran has so far refused to do until the U.S. accepts its core demands to end its naval blockade, ensure a halt to fighting on all fronts in the Middle East, and ease sanctions.
 During the Rezaei-Putin meeting in Moscow on Thursday, the Russian Foreign Ministry warned Russian citizens against all travel to Iran. 
 A pool photograph distributed by the Russian state agency Sputnik shows Russian President Vladimir Putin shaking hands with Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, ahead of talks in Moscow, Nov. 5, 2026. 
 Alexey BABUSHKIN/POOL/AFP/Getty
 "Given the continued risk of a new escalation around Iran, our recommendations to Russian citizens remain unchanged," ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova told reporters in Moscow. "We recommend temporarily refraining from traveling to that country until the situation is resolved. We also ask our compatriots already in Iran to exercise vigilance and avoid crowds, public events, and areas near military and government facilities."
 She said the guidance was "based on the official information disseminated by Tehran," without providing any further detail. 
 By
 Tucker Reals 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-midterms-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-6112d35c 
 link copied 
 9:10 AM / November 5, 2026
 Iran again claims it has no role in backing the Houthis in Yemen's civil war
 The Iranian Foreign Ministry renewed the regime's rejection on Thursday of longtime and widely held beliefs that Tehran materially supports the Houthi rebels fighting the Saudi Arabia-backed government in Yemen's decade-long civil war. The conflict intensified a couple months ago and quickly became the most active and deadly front in the intertwined conflicts in the Middle East.
 Foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei called the latest accusation of Iranian support for the Houthis, made Monday by European Union foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas, "baseless," and said Iran "strongly denied claims that Iranian military experts were present in Yemen."
 The U.S. government, along with many other Western nations and the NATO alliance , have demanded for years that Iran stop supporting the Houthis. The support, according to these nations, includes financial backing, weapons and other equipment, and direct coordination and training.
 In July, not long before the Yemen war escalated and the Houthis started launching attacks on Saudi airports in response, the Reuters news agency reported that Iran  had flown commanders from its powerful, heavily  sanctioned Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, along with equipment related to missiles and drones, to Yemen bolster the Houthis' ability to threaten global energy supplies in the Red Sea.
 Since then, Houthi missile strikes on Saudi Arabian airports have killed at least 20 people. 
 In her remarks Monday, the EU's Kallas said "all Houthi military action must end immediately. We call on all actors, including Iran to cease all military support to the Houthis, in violation of several United Nations Security Council resolutions."
 Iran has always denied supporting the Houthis.
 By
 Tucker Reals 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-midterms-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-ffccea0b 
 link copied 
 7:59 AM / November 5, 2026
 Oman says still working with Iran on joint control system for Strait of Hormuz "that would end the state of war"
 Oman's government said Thursday that, in a phone call between the Omani and Iranian foreign ministers, both men "stressed the importance of moving from the stage of de-escalating tensions to one of establishing sustainable understandings based on practical arrangements to ensure the safety of maritime routes and joint technical mechanisms to secure the smooth flow of international trade and energy, in a manner that would end the state of war and prevent renewed confrontations in the region."
 Omani Foreign Minister Sayyid Badr bin Hamad bin Hamoud Al Busaidi and his Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi "reviewed the latest developments in communications and discussions aimed at reaching practical, political, and technical understandings that would enable the resumption of unimpeded maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz," the Omani Foreign Ministry said in a statement .
 Iran and Oman have discussed for months implementing a joint mechanism to control commercial traffic through the strait, over which both Iran and the U.S. insist they currently have dominion. Iran started threatening and attacking ships in the region in response to the U.S. and Israel jointly launching the ongoing war against the Islamic Republic at the end of February, and those attacks continue despite U.S. assertions that the strait is now open safe to use.
 CBS News
 According to Oman, the ministers emphasized in their Thursday call that any future "understandings must be based on respect for the sovereignty of states, consideration of the legitimate interests of all parties, and the creation of appropriate conditions for restoring dialogue and negotiation processes and addressing the outstanding issues underlying the escalation."
 By
 Tucker Reals 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-midterms-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-53cf1f6f 
 link copied 
 5:40 AM / November 5, 2026
 Another oil tanker hits mine, catches fire near Strait of Hormuz, Iran says
 An oil tanker hit a mine, caught fire and was immobilized east of the Strait of Hormuz early on Thursday, Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corp navy said, according to IRNA, Tehran's official news agency.
 The navy said the tanker had switched off its identification and navigation systems, a tactic used by vessels seeking to avoid detection by Iran.
 The IRGC has declared the strait "unsafe and closed" to vessels trying to go through the vital waterway without coordination with Tehran.
 By
 Brian Dakss 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-midterms-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-fa2ac7e1 
 link copied 
 5:17 AM / November 5, 2026
 Saudi coalition says it intercepted Houthi missile fired at Medina region
 The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthi rebels said on Thursday that a ballistic missile fired by the group at the Medina region — home to one of Islam's holiest cities — had been intercepted. 
 "Air defense intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the terrorist Houthi militia toward the Medina region," coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki said in a social media post.
 By
 AFP 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-midterms-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-1fe9c81a 
 link copied 
 3:46 AM / November 5, 2026
 Tanker hit by 2 projectiles north of Qatar, British military says
 A tanker was hit by two unidentified projectiles in the Persian Gulf about 50 nautical miles north of Madinat ash Shamal, Qatar, a British military tracking agency said Thursday.
 The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Centre (KKMTO) said the status of the crew, damage assessment and environmental impact weren't known.  
 By
 Brian Dakss 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-midterms-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-833dedfe 
 link copied 
 2:33 AM / November 5, 2026
 Iran says two tankers and tugboat caught fire in Strait of Hormuz
 Two oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps said, local media reported on Thursday. 
 Since the outbreak of the Iran war on Feb. 28, Tehran has severely restricted traffic through the strategic waterway, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption. 
 In response, the United States has imposed a blockade on Iranian ports and helped tankers travel through the strait. The U.S. Central Command said last month that it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via the strait since summer. 
 "Last night, in two separate incidents, a large oil tanker attempting to pass through the illegal passageway south of the Strait of Hormuz suffered a fire after striking a mine and was brought to a halt," the Guard told Iran's Fars news agency. 
 "Another supertanker was halted by a massive fire while exiting the eastern Strait of Hormuz. A tugboat that had approached the supertanker to extinguish the fire also caught fire." 
 Fars also reported the IRGC navy's electronic warfare unit had taken control of two LUCAS drones, a U.S.-developed model short for Low-cost Uncrewed Combat Attack System. 
 By
 AFP 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-midterms-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-d5a6c6c5 
 link copied 
 7:07 PM / November 4, 2026
 Reelected Colorado Rep. Jason Crow on Iran after midterms: "The war has got to end"
 Colorado Democratic Rep. Jason Crow, who has won his midterm reelection bid, told CBS News how Democrats will address the war with Iran as the party takes control of Congress next year, saying, "The war has got to end."
 "Americans never wanted it to begin with. Americans for years have wanted to end this constant cycle of conflict in the Middle East. In fact, Donald Trump even campaigned on that," Crow, a member of the House Armed Services Committee, told Major Garrett on "The Takeout" on Wednesday night.
 Asked whether Congress plans to address the war through war power resolutions or
 using the power of appropriations to take away funding, Crow replied: "Yes."
 "We have voted on seven resolutions and passed two of them so far. We should continue to take votes. Let people stand up," he added. "Appropriations is one of our most powerful tools. We have to be willing to do that too."
 When it comes to the future of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, Crow said that future "should be short."
 "Pete Hegseth is incompetent. He was never qualified to do this, never should have been in the position to begin with. He needs to go," he said.
 By
 Kiki Intarasuwan 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-midterms-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-dd7029ae 
 link copied 
 2:33 PM / November 4, 2026
 U.S. sanctions Indian companies over alleged maritime fraud aiding Iran
 The United States on Wednesday issued sanctions targeting what it described as a "vast criminal network" run by two Indian nationals that was aiding Iran's shadow fleet of oil tankers in committing maritime fraud.
 In a statement, the U.S. Treasury said the network aided Iranian vessels in sailing under false flags and in gaining fake maritime certifications.
 The move was the latest in a tightening web of U.S. sanctions targeting Iran since August, when Washington announced it would be seeking the "economic asphyxiation" of the country in conjunction with its military campaign.
 "As we have said many times, under Operation Economic Outcast, you are either with us or against us," said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who has in the past threatened sanctions against any country or company that aids Iran, regardless of its relationship with Washington.
 Wednesday's sanctions named Indian nationals Suniel Kumar Sharma and his wife Jaspreet Preeti Shahid as operating a large-scale maritime fraud network from their base in Chandigarh.
 "Purporting to represent nations from nearly every continent, from Guyana to Eswatini and Laos, Sharma and Shahid have allowed the Iranian shadow fleet ... to evade international restrictions on their operation," the Treasury said in a statement.
 By
 AFP 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-midterms-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-43605b9d 
 link copied 
 2:05 PM / November 4, 2026
 Head of Iran's Supreme National Security Council takes shot at U.S. in wake of election
The powerful head of the Iranian Supreme National Security Council gave credit to his country for the rebuke of President Trump in the midterm elections. 
"The Iranian nation handed Trump a strategic defeat on the battlefield and in the Hormuz — and a POLITICAL DEFEAT in Washington," Mohsen Rezaei said on X . "Meanwhile, Americans got stuck with the bill for his war." 
"Anyone who takes on Iran will pay the price — from the battlefield to their own doorstep," he added. 
Vice President JD Vance reportedly reached out to Rezaei last week about discussing conditions for a ceasefire and negotiations on the war. It's unclear how the midterm elections will affect Iran's negotiations to end the war, but President Trump said he did not regret the attacks. 
 By
 Mark Osborne 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-midterms-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-d88de67a 
 link copied 
 1:46 PM / November 4, 2026
 Following Democratic wave, Schumer says war in Iran "must end"
 Top Senate Democrat Chuck Schumer said Wednesday that the Iran war "must end" and suggested his party's incoming majority in Congress could use their control over government funding to press for that goal.
 "The American people don't know what the heck we're fighting for in Iran," Schumer told journalists. "He's never made it clear he changes his mind day to day and minute to minute. This war must end. It must end."
 He later noted the "power of the purse" is "one of the ways of deterring a president who does war without the consent of the American people."
 Schumer and Democrats in Congress have been pushing to pass war powers resolutions throughout the war. The bills would force President Trump to remove soldiers from Iran.
 The longtime New York Democrat also intimated funding could be pulled in order to force the war to come to an end. 
 Exit polls showed most think the U.S. made the wrong decision to take that military action, including about a quarter of Republicans.
 AFP/CBS 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-midterms-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-c69a9db9 
 link copied 
 1:29 PM / November 4, 2026
 Trump says it's "largely true" the war in Iran cost Republicans in midterms
 President Trump said it's "probably true" the war in Iran was responsible for heavy Republican losses in the midterm elections, specifically the cost of gas related to the war.
 "Well, I think it's largely true because it drove the gasoline up a little bit short term," he told reporters at an event related to the ballroom's construction. "But at the same time, if I had it to do again, I'd have to do it again. Because long term, it's the only answer. You can't let Iran have a nuclear weapon."
 Mr. Trump was responding to a question about Vice President JD Vance blaming the losses on the war in a post on X earlier in the day.
 "But I can tell you that as far as that war is concerned, I would have done nothing different," Trump continued. "We've totally broken their military. The navy's gone. Their air force is gone. Their anti-aircraft is gone."
 By
 Mark Osborne 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-midterms-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-2cf1b0d2 
 link copied 
 12:50 PM / November 4, 2026
 Red Cross delivers first supplies to Yemen's Taiz in over a month
 The International Committee of the Red Cross said it delivered medical supplies into Taiz on Wednesday for the first time in weeks since the Iran-backed Houthis surrounded the Yemeni city.
 The ICRC "delivered four trucks of essential medical supplies to Taiz city, including surgical kits to help hospitals treat weapon-wounded patients," it said in a statement. "This is the ICRC's first delivery of medical supplies to hospitals in Taiz City since 23 September, just before the intensification of fighting in the area."
 Taiz, which is located in western Yemen, has become the focal point of the war between the Iran-backed Houthis and Saudi-backed Yemeni army. In late summer, the Houthis swept through the western part of the country and acquired wide swaths of land up to the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, which forms the southern opening to the Red Sea.
 Taiz, the country's third-largest city, was left isolated from international aid groups when the Houthis rapidly took over the territory. 
 AFP/CBS 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-midterms-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-1ca9c07a 
 link copied 
 12:12 PM / November 4, 2026
 Brent crude drops under $100, lowest level since September
 Brent crude oil, the international standard, dropped significantly on Wednesday, falling under $100 a barrel for the first time since September.
 The price was down over 8% at noon Eastern time, falling to about $94 a barrel. The cost hasn't been under $95 a barrel since Sept. 1.
 Brent crude last closed at under $100 a barrel on Sept. 30. The cost then consistently rose to a high of $116 per barrel on Oct. 23. It has dropped since, closing at $103 per barrel on Tuesday.
 The decrease comes a day after Democrats won by a landslide in midterm elections, rebuking President Trump and his position on the war with Iran. Democrats, who have already voted several times in the House to restore war powers to Congress, are likely to pursue de-escalation in the conflict.
 By
 Mark Osborne 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-midterms-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-44e75e86 
 link copied 
 11:45 AM / November 4, 2026
 Trump asking advisers if Pete Hegseth should go, sources say
 President Trump has been asking advisers around him and on the phone whether Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth should stay in his job, following Republicans' catastrophic losses Tuesday night, multiple sources familiar with the matter tell CBS News.
 Some White House aides have predicted some of the blame for GOP midterm losses will be trained on Adm. Brad Cooper, the head of U.S. Central Command, and Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Gen. Dan Caine, who both played big roles in guidance on the Iran war.
 Still, other sources said the president hasn't decided to replace Hegseth. Before the election, Democrats were already trying to impeach Hegseth, and the likelihood of an impeachment effort could increase with Democrats holding strong majorities in both chambers.
 Read more here .
 By
 Jennifer Jacobs 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-midterms-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-ad041210 
 link copied 
 11:30 AM / November 4, 2026
 Vance blames Iran conflict for GOP midterm defeats: "The reason we lost is the war"
 In his first public comments on the election results, Vice President JD Vance said the reason Republicans were handedly defeated in the House and Senate is because of the war in Iran.
 "The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night," Vance wrote in a post on X . "If you'd like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so. Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that's at least honest. But everyone knows why we lost. And any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there."
 The vice president, a possible 2028 contender, said many voters who backed the Trump-Vance ticket in 2024 cast their ballots for Democrats in 2026 for four reasons: to end the war with Iran, focus on the cost of living and inflation, put America first and change the U.S. relationship with Israel.
 "Our voters showed up," Vance wrote. "And the above four reasons are why many of them voted for Democrats."
 Read more here .
 By
 Melissa Quinn 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-midterms-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-817220c8 
 link copied

 Iran claims to have shot down another U.S. MQ-1 drone over island in Strait of Hormuz
 Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said in a statement Wednesday it had shot down a U.S. MQ-1 drone over Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, claiming it was the 15th of the type downed by Iranian forces during the war.
 In September, U.S. officials told CBS News on condition of anonymity that Iranian forces had, at that time, brought down at least two MQ-1s. 
 The U.S. military has fielded two principal MQ-1 variants: the Predator, which became a fixture of U.S. operations in Iraq and Afghanistan before the Air Force retired it in 2018, and the Gray Eagle, a larger Predator-derived aircraft still operated by the Army, including its special operations forces.
 Both the Predator and Gray Eagle were designed for intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance missions but they can also carry Hellfire missiles for striking targets. In the Strait of Hormuz, these unmanned aircraft can provide U.S. forces with persistent surveillance over the narrow waterway while also tracking Iranian military activity and monitoring threats to both American forces and commercial shipping.
 The Air Force's older MQ-1 Predators have largely been retired, but if Iran has in fact shot down 10 of the aircraft, the loss would still equate to roughly $40 million.

 The Lebanon conflict has proven to be a major sticking point in negotiations between the U.S. and Iran, as Tehran has consistently rejected any peace deal with Washington that does not also end fighting in Lebanon and Gaza.
